resources.string: Android audio, sampled on Ableton Move

iPhones already send audio to Move over USB-C. Most Android phones only show Move as a MIDI controller. Move Bridge gives Android the same ability, so anything playing on your phone can be sampled on Move.
Connect with a USB-C data cable
Press the wheel until it shows USB-C
Press a pad to record, press it again to stop
To hear the phone through the Move while sampling, turn monitoring on: select the headphones icon on the Move\'s screen and press the wheel.
Plug in and audio starts. No screens in between.
For the screen-share method: approve once per phone restart. Android shows its capture icon while ready.

To send your phone\'s sound to the Move, Android needs its capture permission. Android calls this “sharing your screen”. Move Bridge never records or sends your screen: it only takes the audio and sends it straight to the Move over the cable.
On the next screen, tap Start.
Tap Start again and allow Move Bridge to use the Move.
Plug the Move into your phone with a USB-C data cable.
Move Bridge needs it to pick up your phone\'s sound.

It lets Android play straight to your Move: the least delay and no screen-sharing prompt. Tap for the guide (about two minutes).
Needed once after a phone restart. Tap to open Developer options. Or turn on Start automatically below, and Move Bridge does it for you next time.
After a phone restart, Move Bridge briefly turns Wireless debugging on to start its helper again, then off. Needs Wi-Fi.
The phone\'s speaker plays too, together with the Move. The phone\'s volume then sets the level for both. Changes right away.
Settings → About phone → Software information → tap Build number 7 times. Then come back to Move Bridge.

Check the code and try again. If the pairing screen closed, open it again; a new code is shown.
You can leave Wireless debugging. Plug in the Move and play something.

The Move is now your phone\'s audio output, like USB-C headphones. The phone\'s volume buttons set the level. On the Move: Sampling → USB-C, then hold a pad.
Phone audio plays on the Move
440 Hz tone through Android\'s own output. On the Move, set Sampling input to USB-C. Too quiet? Turn the phone\'s volume up.

Play anything on your phone. On the Move: Sampling → USB-C, then hold a pad.
Tip: turn the phone\'s media volume all the way up. The Move records at the phone\'s volume.
Audio will start as soon as the Move connects.
Puts the phone on vibrate while audio goes to the Move, so rings and pings don\'t land in your samples. Alarms still sound.
A one-time setup, about two minutes, lets Android play straight to your Move: the least delay, no screen-sharing prompt, and nothing to tap when you plug in.
Pair Move Bridge with a code
In About phone, open Software information and tap Build number 7 times. Then come back here.

In Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging (the phone must be on Wi-Fi) and tap Allow. Then open Wireless debugging and tap Pair device with pairing code. Keep that screen open, pull down your notifications, and type the 6-digit code into the Move Bridge notification.
Open Wireless debugging and tap Pair device with pairing code. Keep that screen open, pull down your notifications, and type the 6-digit code into the Move Bridge notification.
Paired. Tap Start now. If it doesn\'t start, turn Wireless debugging on once more.
All set. Plug in your Move and play something.
Not now: use screen sharing instead

Android only lets its own debugging service start the small helper that Move Bridge needs to route audio. Move Bridge connects only to this phone itself, never to another device, and you can turn Wireless debugging off again afterwards.

• Simpler settings. The Audio-only mode and Direct to Move switches are gone: once the one-time setup is done, Move Bridge always plays straight to the Move.

• If the setup isn't done yet, or Wireless debugging is needed after a restart, Settings tells you what to do.

• The steps on the Move now match Ableton's manual, with a tip about monitoring.

• Open-source licenses are listed at the bottom of the main screen.
Move Bridge is in beta. Tell us what works and what doesn\'t: that decides what gets fixed next. Nothing is sent unless you send it.
What works, what doesn\'t, what\'s missing: every note helps make Move Bridge better for Move owners.

Move Bridge has no accounts, no ads and no tracking, and it never sends anything by itself. A report only leaves your phone when you send it from this screen, and you can read every line of it first. Reports are used to fix and improve Move Bridge, and for nothing else.
